paragraph:
Culture on the hoof
A rural festival discovers the difference between attracting an audience and sustaining a place

In the fictional district of Harth, a windswept (plateau) is to become the setting for an international arts festival. The organisers promise to (endow) the countryside with a new economic purpose. Farmers wonder what was wrong with the old one. The dispute is less about culture than about who gets paid.

The festival's (protagonist) is a retired promoter, an (optimist) whose appetite for projects has survived several failures. He wants to (enlist) local businesses in a campaign to put Harth on the cultural map. His presentation contains a (slew) of forecasts and a (prolix) account of his connections. The village plumber asks about toilets.

That question identifies the central (flaw). A festival can generate demand faster than a district can (adjust) its services. Visitors may (overflow) into nearby settlements, while delivery vehicles block the only (roundabout). The promoter calls this momentum. Residents call it Thursday.

The proposed site is a former farm on the (purlieu) of the market town. Its fields (abut) a stream, and a shepherd's (hut) will become a ticket office. Volunteers clear (sawdust) from a workshop and turn garden waste into (compost). Such improvements are useful, although a fresh coat of paint is not a business model.

The farm has its own calendar. Workers must (harrow) one field and plant (flax) in another; leaving everything (fallow) has a cost. A (sow) is expected to (farrow) during opening week. Nobody has explained to her that contemporary dance is the district's new priority.

A more sensible plan would treat farming as an asset. A grower displaying a prize (marrow) could share a stall with a baker discussing the perfect (crust). A conservation volunteer could show children a (minnow) in the stream. Rural life need not become a quaint (sideshow) to imported entertainment.

The programme nevertheless spans the entire (gamut) of cultural ambition. A (philatelist) displays stamps, a (numismatist) brings coins, and a (taxonomist) explains how classification changes knowledge. An artist exhibits a (woodcut) beside a carved (amethyst). The festival's virtue is its variety; its danger is confusing accumulation with coherence.

At the opening, a (percussionist) performs an (impromptu) solo. A retired (pugilist) describes a memorable (bout), while a (podiatrist) advises walkers about footwear. An acrobat with a bandaged (wrist) cancels her appearance. Expertise, it turns out, is not interchangeable merely because everyone wears a performer’s pass.

The promoter's favourite designer proposes a pavilion with a (convex) roof and a sharp (vertex) above the entrance. Its model resembles a three-dimensional (jigsaw). A carpenter points to a missing (screw) and asks how the frame will resist a strong (gust). Structural questions can spoil an architectural (debut), but gravity is an unforgiving critic.

Transport offers similar lessons. A publicity drone begins to (yaw) above the car park. A hired shuttle takes a circuitous route through three villages. Its driver, unlike the marketing team, understands that the landscape cannot be rearranged for convenience. Local (know-how) is the (sinew) of the enterprise.

The first tickets sell briskly. A travel (guru) describes Harth as an antidote to metropolitan fatigue, appealing to (wanderlust) without mentioning the limited accommodation. Hotels (tout) premium packages; homeowners discover a sudden (lust) for rental income. A village that was a minor tourism destination briefly imagines itself a commercial (juggernaut).

Early success can (skew) judgement. Organisers commission extra shows, creating a (glut) of seats on quieter afternoons. Discounted tickets (undercut) village events that receive no subsidy. The promoter calls anyone who questions the forecasts a (defeatist). An unsold seat, however, is not an ideological objection.

Nor does attendance guarantee prosperity. An artist may receive applause and still struggle to (subsist). Caterers can (exhaust) their cash buying stock before customers arrive. A sponsor may (withdraw) after the invoices fall due. If the venture goes (bust), enthusiasm will prove a poor substitute for working capital.

Politics soon supplies its own entertainment. A (conformist) councillor praises the scheme because the party does; a (nonconformist) opposes it for much the same reason. An online (extremist) wants to (overthrow) the entire council. A petition merely seeks to (oust) the chair of the festival committee. Proportion is the first casualty of a village argument.

The promoter, increasingly irritable, calls a critic an (egotist); she replies that he is a (narcissist). A columnist makes both the (butt) of a joke. These exchanges (overshadow) a useful dispute over public guarantees. Personalities are easier to describe than liabilities, which is why the former get more coverage.

Residents have legitimate concerns. A drunken (lout) may (accost) a passer-by, or an impatient visitor may (elbow) someone out of a queue. A noise (curfew) is therefore reasonable. Officials should neither (cow) complainants into silence nor pretend that every expression of (disgust) establishes a case for cancellation.

The audience itself resists easy labels. A (hedonist) wants food and music; a (devout) churchgoer attends a choral concert; a (highbrow) visitor prefers a lecture. The organiser should (eschew) the assumption that one group can (bestow) legitimacy on the others. A good festival accommodates differences without requiring everyone to like everything.

One exhibition demands particular care. It commemorates a wartime (holocaust) that destroyed a distant town, using survivors' testimony. Its (august) curator insists on context and a quiet room. Placing a drinks promotion beside it would be more than bad taste. The urge to (hallow) suffering should not become an excuse to package it carelessly.

Elsewhere, the environmental programme examines a (locust) outbreak through photographs and interviews. Another installation traces water from a spring (thaw) to the (nethermost) chamber of an old mine. These works can (foreshadow) difficult questions about land use. They need not offer a reassuring ending to justify their place.

The festival's own ending arrives with a (cloudburst). Mud replaces the advertised evening (glow), and a (stout) volunteer helps drag equipment uphill. A (callow) assistant begins to (pout) when his livestream fails, then makes himself useful carrying cables. Competence is acquired less glamorously than publicity suggests.

The intended (climax), a concert on the hill's (apex), becomes an (anticlimax) in a school hall. Yet this is not a complete (rout). Local musicians perform, the kitchen stays open and strangers talk. What looked like a damaged product becomes, briefly, an actual gathering.

The council should now (winnow) the useful results from the inflated claims. The next plan ought to (avow) its costs, (disavow) impossible promises and explain the (thrust) of each subsidy. Questions about money will continue to (vex) organisers. They are precisely the questions that can make a second festival possible.
translation:
田野上的文化生意
一场乡村节庆发现，吸引观众与维系一个地方并非一回事

在虚构的哈思地区，一片风吹不息的(高原)即将成为国际艺术节的举办地。主办方承诺，为乡村(赋予)一种新的经济使命。农民们想知道，原来的使命究竟有什么问题。这场争论与其说关乎文化，不如说关乎谁能拿到钱。

艺术节的(主角)是一位退休的活动推广人，也是一个经历数次失败后仍热衷项目的(乐观主义者)。他想(动员)本地企业参与行动，让哈思在文化版图上占有一席之地。他的演示包含(大量)预测，以及对自己人脉的(冗长)介绍。村里的水管工问起了厕所。

这个问题指出了核心(缺陷)。节庆创造需求的速度，可能超过地区(调整)服务的速度。游客可能(涌入)附近聚落，送货车辆则堵住唯一的(环岛)。推广人称这是发展势头。居民称这是星期四。

拟议场地是一座位于集镇(边缘地带)的旧农场。田地(毗邻)一条溪流，牧羊人的(小屋)将被改成售票处。志愿者清理工坊里的(木屑)，把园艺废料变成(堆肥)。这些改善很有用，只是刷上一层新漆并不等于建立了商业模式。

农场有自己的时间表。工人必须(耙平)一块田地，在另一块种植(亚麻)；让所有土地都(休耕)，是有成本的。一头(母猪)预计将在开幕周(产仔)。还没有人向它解释，当代舞已经成为本地区的新优先事项。

更明智的计划会把农业视为资产。展示获奖(大西葫芦)的种植者，可以与讨论完美面包(外皮)的烘焙师共用一个摊位。自然保护志愿者可以带孩子观察溪流中的(鲦鱼)。乡村生活不必沦为外来娱乐旁边一项古朴的(附带表演)。

不过，节目仍覆盖了文化抱负的整个(范围)。一位(集邮者)展示邮票，一位(钱币收藏家)带来硬币，一位(分类学家)解释分类如何改变知识。一名艺术家将(木刻版画)与雕琢过的(紫水晶)并列展出。艺术节的优点在于多样性，危险则在于把堆积误当成连贯。

开幕时，一位(打击乐手)进行了一段(即兴的)独奏。一位退休(拳击手)讲述一场难忘的(拳赛)，一位(足病医生)则向步行者提供鞋履建议。一名(手腕)缠着绷带的杂技演员取消了演出。事实证明，不能因为人人都挂着表演者通行证，就认为专业能力可以相互替代。

推广人最喜欢的设计师提出建造一座展亭，屋顶(向外凸起)，入口上方有一个尖锐的(顶点)。模型像一副立体(拼图)。木匠指着一处缺失的(螺丝)，问框架如何抵挡强烈的(阵风)。结构问题可能破坏建筑的(首次亮相)，但重力是一位毫不留情的评论家。

交通也提供了类似的教训。一架宣传无人机开始在停车场上方(偏航)。租来的接驳车绕行三个村庄。与营销团队不同，司机明白，地形不能为了方便而重新排列。本地(实务知识)是这项事业的(力量支柱)。

首批门票销售迅速。一位旅游(大师)将哈思描述为都市疲惫的解药，迎合人们的(旅行欲)，却不提住宿有限。酒店(兜售)高端套餐，房主突然发现自己对租金收入产生了(强烈渴望)。这个原本不起眼的旅游村庄，一时把自己想象成商业(巨无霸)。

早期成功可能(扭曲)判断。主办方追加演出，结果在冷清的下午出现座位(供过于求)。折扣票以更低价格(挤压)了没有补贴的村庄活动。推广人把所有质疑预测的人都称作(失败主义者)。然而，一张卖不出去的座位，并不是某种意识形态上的反对意见。

到场人数也不能保证繁荣。艺术家可能收获掌声，却仍难以(维持生计)。餐饮商可能在顾客到来前，就因采购存货而(耗尽)现金。赞助商可能在账单到期后(退出)。如果项目最终(破产)，热情将被证明远远不能替代营运资金。

政治很快贡献了自己的娱乐。一位(墨守成规者)议员因为政党支持而赞扬计划；一位(不随大流者)则出于几乎相同的原因反对。一名网络(极端分子)想要(推翻)整个议会。一份请愿书仅要求(赶下台)艺术节委员会主席。分寸感是村庄争论中最先牺牲的东西。

推广人越来越急躁，称一位批评者为(自大者)；她回敬说他是(自恋者)。一位专栏作家让两人都成了笑话的(笑柄)。这些交锋(盖过了)一场有关公共担保的有益争论。性格比负债更容易描述，所以前者获得了更多报道。

居民的担忧有其道理。醉酒的(粗野之徒)可能(上前纠缠)路人，不耐烦的游客也可能用(肘推)的方式把别人挤出队伍。因此，设置噪声(宵禁)是合理的。官员既不应(恐吓)投诉者使其噤声，也不应假装每一次(厌恶)的表达都足以构成取消活动的理由。

观众本身也很难被简单贴上标签。一位(享乐主义者)想要美食和音乐，一位(虔诚的)教徒参加合唱音乐会，一位(趣味高雅的)游客偏爱讲座。主办方应当(摒弃)某个群体能够向其他群体(赐予)正当性的假设。好的节庆容纳差异，不要求所有人喜欢一切。

有一场展览需要格外谨慎。它借助幸存者的证言，纪念一场摧毁远方城镇的战时(浩劫)。其(德高望重的)策展人坚持提供历史背景，并安排安静的展室。在旁边开展酒水促销，就不仅仅是品位欠佳。将苦难(神圣化)的冲动，不应成为草率包装苦难的借口。

别处的环境专题通过照片和访谈，探讨一次(蝗虫)灾害。另一件装置作品追踪水流从春季(解冻)到流入旧矿井(最底层的)洞室的过程。这些作品可以(预示)土地使用方面的棘手问题。它们不必提供令人安心的结局，才能证明自身价值。

艺术节自己的结尾伴随着一场(暴雨)到来。泥泞取代了广告里的傍晚(霞光)，一名(壮实的)志愿者帮忙把设备拖上山坡。一名(稚嫩的)助手在直播失败后开始(噘嘴)，随后转而搬运电缆，总算派上用场。能力的获得，远没有宣传所暗示的那么光鲜。

原定的(高潮)——山丘(最高处)的音乐会——变成了学校礼堂里一个(令人扫兴的结局)。然而，这并非彻底的(溃败)。本地音乐家登台，厨房继续营业，陌生人彼此交谈。原本看似受损的产品，短暂地变成了一场真正的聚会。

议会现在应当从夸大的宣称中(筛选)有用的成果。下一份计划应当(公开承认)成本，(否认并放弃)不可能兑现的承诺，并解释每项补贴的(主旨)。有关金钱的问题将继续(困扰)主办方。而恰恰是这些问题，能够让第二届艺术节成为可能。

本批词根亮点：

• amethyst：a（否定）+ methyst（醉），古希腊人相信紫水晶能防止醉酒，methanol（甲醇）同根

• juggernaut：来自梵语 Jagannath（宇宙之主），印度神车传说信徒被轧死=不可阻挡的力量

• curfew：法语 couvre+feu（盖+火），中世纪每晚敲钟提醒市民盖住炉火=宵禁

• narcissist：来自希腊神话美少年 Narcissus，爱上自己水中倒影，最终化为水仙花

• gamut：来自中世纪音乐中整个音阶的名称（gamma+ut），全音阶=全部范围

• holocaust：holo（全部）+ caust（燃烧），全部焚烧=大浩劫，caustic（腐蚀性）同根

• callow：原意是没长羽毛的雏鸟，引申为幼稚无经验的

• highbrow/lowbrow：来自颅相学，认为额头高=聪明

quiz.question: _____ philatelist
quiz.explanation: 集邮家, 邮票集邮家. The stamp philatelist collected rare postage items. 邮票集邮家收集稀有邮政物品。 | philos->热爱，atelia->免税（希腊，ateleia->免邮费），philatelist->热爱免费邮票的人=集邮家（cf. philosophy哲学，philanthropy慈善） || 文化联想：中国人熟悉的集邮册最适合帮助记忆 philatelist，可以说 **a dedicated philatelist — “A dedicated philatelist may spend years collecting rare Chinese stamps and organizing them by date and issue.”**

quiz.question: pugilist ________
quiz.explanation: 拳击手, 拳击冠军. The pugilist champion defended his title successfully. 拳击冠军成功卫冕。 | pugil->拳击手（拉丁pugnus->拳头），pugilist->用拳头战斗的人=拳击手（cf. pugnacious好斗，impugn质疑，repugnant令人厌恶） || 文化联想：中国拳击比赛里的职业拳手最适合帮助记忆 pugilist，可以说 **a seasoned pugilist — “A seasoned pugilist may rely on footwork, timing, and defense rather than simply throwing harder punches.”**

quiz.question: enlist _______
quiz.explanation: 征募; 争取, 争取支持. The campaign will enlist support from local businesses. 该活动将争取当地企业的支持。 | en->使，list->名单，enlist->把名字列入名单=征募/争取（cf. list列表，enroll注册，conscript征召，recruit招募） || 文化联想：中文“争取大家支持”最适合帮助记忆 enlist，可以说 **enlist support — “A community project may enlist support from local businesses, volunteers, and neighborhood groups.”**

quiz.question: _______ extremist
quiz.explanation: 极端主义者, 暴力极端主义者. The violent extremist was arrested by authorities. 暴力极端主义者被当局逮捕。 | extrem->极端（拉丁extremus->最外端的），extremist->持极端立场的人（cf. extreme极端，external外部，exterior外面） || 文化联想：中文“走向极端的人”最适合帮助记忆 extremist，可以说 **a violent extremist — “Authorities may investigate a violent extremist who advocates attacks on civilians.”**

quiz.question: ____ optimist
quiz.explanation: 乐观主义者, 天生的乐观主义者. She is a born optimist who sees the bright side. 她是一个天生的乐观主义者,总看到光明的一面。 | optim->最好（拉丁optimus），optimist->相信事情最好的人=乐观主义者（cf. optimal最优，optimize优化，optimum最佳） || 文化联想：中文“凡事都往好处想”最适合帮助记忆 optimist，可以说 **a born optimist — “A born optimist may see a failed exam as a chance to learn rather than a permanent setback.”**

quiz.question: _____ taxonomist
quiz.explanation: 分类学家, 植物分类学家. The plant taxonomist identified new species. 植物分类学家鉴定了新物种。 | taxo->排列（希腊taxis），nom->法则，taxonomist->按法则排列的学者=分类学家（cf. taxonomy分类学，syntax句法，tactics战术） || 文化联想：中国植物园给新物种分类的学者最适合帮助记忆 taxonomist，可以说 **a plant taxonomist — “A plant taxonomist may compare leaves, flowers, seeds, and DNA before identifying a new species.”**

quiz.question: ______ conformist
quiz.explanation: 墨守成规者, 社会墨守成规者. The social conformist follows all societal norms. 社会墨守成规者遵循所有社会规范。 | con->共同，form->形式，conformist->跟随共同形式的人=循规蹈矩者（cf. reform改革，transform转变，inform通知） || 文化联想：中文“随大流、守旧规矩的人”最适合帮助记忆 conformist，可以说 **a social conformist — “A social conformist may follow established customs simply because everyone around him does the same.”**

quiz.question: ______ nonconformist
quiz.explanation: 不墨守成规者, 社会不墨守成规者. The social nonconformist rejected traditional values. 社会不墨守成规者拒绝传统价值观。 | non->否定，conformist->循规蹈矩者，nonconformist->不循规蹈矩的人（cf. noncommittal不表态，nonplussed困惑的） || 文化联想：中文“不愿随大流”最适合帮助记忆 nonconformist，可以说 **a social nonconformist — “A social nonconformist may reject a conventional career path and choose a very different way of life.”**

quiz.question: hedonist _________
quiz.explanation: 享乐主义者, 享乐主义生活方式. He pursued a hedonist lifestyle focused on pleasure. 他追求以快乐为中心的享乐主义生活方式。 | hedone->快乐（希腊），hedonist->追求快乐的人（cf. anhedonia无法感受快乐，hedonism享乐主义） || 文化联想：中文“今朝有酒今朝醉”最适合帮助记忆 hedonist，可以说 **a pleasure-seeking hedonist — “A pleasure-seeking hedonist may spend money freely on food, travel, and entertainment while ignoring long-term consequences.”**

quiz.question: _____ protagonist
quiz.explanation: 主角; 主要人物, 故事主角. The story protagonist overcomes many obstacles. 故事主角克服了许多障碍。 | proto->第一（希腊），agon->竞争，protagonist->第一竞争者=主角（cf. antagonist对手，agony痛苦，agonize煎熬） || 文化联想：中国小说或电视剧里的“主角”最适合帮助记忆 protagonist，可以说 **the story’s protagonist — “The story’s protagonist may begin as an ordinary student and gradually become the central figure of the entire drama.”**

quiz.question: ____ percussionist
quiz.explanation: 打击乐器演奏者, 爵士打击乐器演奏者. The jazz percussionist kept perfect rhythm. 爵士打击乐器演奏者保持完美的节奏。 | per->彻底，cuss->打击（拉丁quatere），percussionist->用打击乐演奏的人（cf. concussion脑震荡，percussion打击乐，repercussion影响） || 文化联想：中国民族乐团里的锣鼓演奏者最适合帮助记忆 percussionist，可以说 **a skilled percussionist — “A skilled percussionist in a Chinese orchestra may control gongs, drums, and cymbals with precise timing.”**

quiz.question: podiatrist ______
quiz.explanation: 足病医生, 足病医生诊所. The podiatrist clinic treats foot problems. 足病医生诊所治疗足部问题。 | pod->脚（希腊pous），iatrist->医生，podiatrist->治疗脚的医生（cf. podium讲台=站脚的，tripod三脚架，pediatrician儿科医生） || 文化联想：中国医院足踝门诊最适合帮助记忆 podiatrist，可以说 **consult a podiatrist — “Someone with persistent heel pain may consult a podiatrist for diagnosis and treatment.”**

quiz.question: bestow _____
quiz.explanation: 授予; 给予, 授予荣誉. The university will bestow honor on the graduate. 大学将授予毕业生荣誉。 | be->使，stow->放置，bestow->把某物放置给某人=授予（cf. stow收放，stowage货物放置，stow away偷乘） || 文化联想：中国大学给杰出校友授予荣誉最适合帮助记忆 bestow，可以说 **bestow an honor — “A university may bestow an honor on a scientist whose work has benefited society.”**

quiz.question: avow _____
quiz.explanation: 承认; 公开宣称, 承认罪责. The defendant chose to avow guilt. 被告选择承认罪责。 | a->朝向，vow->誓言（拉丁votum），avow->公开发誓=公开承认（cf. vow誓言，devout虔诚，avowed公开的） || 文化联想：中文“公开承认，不再遮掩”最适合帮助记忆 avow，可以说 **avow responsibility — “A leader may avow responsibility for a failed decision instead of blaming subordinates.”**

quiz.question: disavow _________
quiz.explanation: 否认; 拒绝承认, 否认知情. The official will disavow knowledge of the scandal. 官员将否认知情这起丑闻。 | dis->否定，avow->承认，disavow->否认承认=拒绝承认（cf. avow承认，disown断绝关系，deny否认） || 文化联想：中文“公开否认与某事有关”最适合帮助记忆 disavow，可以说 **disavow knowledge — “An official may disavow knowledge of a secret arrangement and insist that it was never authorized.”**

quiz.question: flax _____
quiz.explanation: 亚麻, 亚麻纤维. Linen is made from flax fiber. 亚麻布由亚麻纤维制成。 | flax->亚麻（古英语fleax），flax->亚麻植物（cf. linen亚麻布，flaxen淡黄色，flexible柔软=像亚麻一样） || 文化联想：中国传统亚麻纺织最适合帮助记忆 flax，可以说 **flax fiber — “Linen cloth is made from flax fiber that is processed, spun, and woven into fabric.”**

quiz.question: _____ _ climax
quiz.explanation: 高潮; 顶点, 达到高潮. The tension will reach a climax in the final act. 紧张气氛将在最后一幕达到高潮。 | climax->梯子（希腊klimax->梯子），climax->爬到最高点=高潮（cf. climb攀爬，climate气候=倾斜的太阳，acclimate适应气候） || 文化联想：中文“剧情终于推到最高点”最适合帮助记忆 climax，可以说 **reach a climax — “The tension in a historical drama may reach a climax when the final secret is revealed.”**

quiz.question: ____ anticlimax
quiz.explanation: 反高潮; 虎头蛇尾, 情节反高潮. The ending was a disappointing plot anticlimax. 结局是令人失望的情节反高潮。 | anti->对抗，climax->高潮，anticlimax->高潮的对立=反高潮/虎头蛇尾（cf. climax高潮，anticlimactic令人失望的） || 文化联想：中文“虎头蛇尾”最适合帮助记忆 anticlimax，可以说 **a disappointing anticlimax — “After two hours of buildup, an ending in which nothing important happens can feel like a disappointing anticlimax.”**

quiz.question: ________ apex
quiz.explanation: 顶点; 最高点, 山顶. Climbers reached the mountain apex at noon. 登山者在中午到达山顶。 | apex->顶点（拉丁，帽子的顶端），apex->最高点（cf. apogee最远点，aphelion远日点，cf. apex predator顶级捕食者） || 文化联想：泰山或华山最高点的概念最适合帮助记忆 apex，可以说 **the mountain apex — “Climbers may reach the mountain apex just before sunrise and look down over the surrounding ridges.”**

quiz.question: ________ vertex
quiz.explanation: 顶点; 角的顶点, 三角形顶点. The triangle vertex is labeled point A. 三角形顶点标记为A点。 | vert->转（拉丁vertere），vertex->旋转的顶端=顶点（cf. vortex漩涡，vertical垂直，vertigo眩晕=旋转感） || 文化联想：中国中学几何课里的三角形顶点最适合帮助记忆 vertex，可以说 **a triangle vertex — “A geometry teacher may label each triangle vertex with a different capital letter.”**

quiz.question: vex ___ ______
quiz.explanation: 使烦恼; 使恼怒, 使公众烦恼. The controversy will vex the public for months. 这场争议将使公众烦恼数月。 | vex->骚扰（拉丁vexare->摇晃），vex->使烦恼（cf. vexation烦恼，vexatious令人烦恼的，vexed question棘手问题） || 文化联想：中文“这件事让公众烦了几个月”最适合帮助记忆 vex，可以说 **vex the public — “Repeated delays and contradictory announcements may vex the public for months.”**

quiz.question: convex ______
quiz.explanation: 凸的; 凸面的, 凸面镜. The convex mirror provides a wide view. 凸面镜提供广阔的视野。 | con->共同，vex->拱起（拉丁vehere->携带），convex->向外拱起的=凸的（cf. concave凹面，convex凸面，excavate挖掘） || 文化联想：中国停车场或路口的凸面镜最适合帮助记忆 convex，可以说 **a convex mirror — “A convex mirror at a blind corner gives drivers a wider view of approaching traffic.”**

quiz.question: prolix ______
quiz.explanation: 冗长的; 啰嗦的, 冗长的演讲. His prolix speech bored the audience. 他冗长的演讲使观众感到厌烦。 | pro->向前，lix->流动（拉丁liqui），prolix->话语像水一样流个不停=冗长的（cf. liquid液体，liquor酒，prolixity啰嗦） || 文化联想：中文“又臭又长、啰里啰嗦”最适合帮助记忆 prolix，可以说 **a prolix speech — “A prolix speech may bury one simple idea under forty minutes of unnecessary explanation.”**
